chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:

I said to him: One who does not know whether he is in four or in two, while he has secured the two—he said: “He performs two rakʿahs and four sajdahs while standing with Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, and he recites the tashahhud, and there is nothing upon him. And if he does not know whether he is in three or in four, while he has secured the three, he stands and adds another to it, and there is nothing upon him. Certainty is not overturned by doubt, nor is doubt entered into certainty, nor should one mix one of them with the other; rather, he overturns doubt by certainty and completes upon certainty, so he builds upon it, and he does not give consideration to doubt in any state among the states.”

key_terms.الشَّكِّ: doubt concerning the number of prayer units
key_terms.الْيَقِينَ: certainty regarding what has definitely been performed
key_terms.بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: with Sūrat al-Fātiḥah recited in the prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs to be performed in the described case of doubt
key_terms.سَجَدَاتٍ: prostrations performed as part of the prayer units
key_terms.فَيَبْنِي عَلَيْهِ: he bases his action upon that certainty

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat (prayer) if they doubt the number of rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for doubt in salat (prayer), instructing the worshipper to build on what is certain when uncertain about the number of rakʿahs. It establishes the principle that certainty is not overturned by doubt, which is a foundational rule in Shia jurisprudence.
